expected.finding: **[P1]** Secret sanitization still leaks credentials into reports and workflow logs. In [mine-trace-failures.py:255](/home/runner/work/open-inspect-72e95a/open-inspect-72e95a/scripts/mine-trace-failures.py:255), truncation happens before redaction: a long database URL loses its trailing `@`, preventing password detection. Additionally, [improvement_policy.py:105](/home/runner/work/open-inspect-72e95a/open-inspect-72e95a/scripts/improvement_policy.py:105) misses quoted JSON keys such as `{"password": "[REDACTED]"}`. Both leaks reproduced. Scrub complete text before truncating and cover quoted credential fields.

**[P2]** Merged failures backdate newly observed evidence. [mine-trace-failures.py:265](/home/runner/work/open-inspect-72e95a/open-inspect-72e95a/scripts/mine-trace-failures.py:265) appends later diagnostics while retaining the first occurrence’s timestamp. A credential diagnostic appearing at time 100 consequently counts in the historical anchor at time 50 when merged with a failure from time 1. Preserve the first matching timestamp per topic so historical validity cannot use future evidence.

**[P2]** The new deduplication regression test fails and never exercises its intended branch. In [mine_trace_failures_test.py:521](/home/runner/work/open-inspect-72e95a/open-inspect-72e95a/scripts/mine_trace_failures_test.py:521), `token expired` changes the second failure’s kind to `auth`, producing a different excerpt and deduplication key. The assertion expecting one merged failure fails both independently and in the full suite. Use later diagnostics that preserve the failure kind and excerpt.

+def scrub_secrets(text: str) -> str:
+    """Replace credential-shaped substrings with [REDACTED], keeping the

+        if pattern.groups:
+            text = pattern.sub(

+                text,
+            )
+        else:
+            text = pattern.sub("[REDACTED]", text)
+    return text
